data.decode#decode: github.com/go-avkit/decode (v0.1.0) decodes H.264 to planar YUV, in pure Go with no cgo. The decoding itself is oops1/go.264 (BSD-2-Clause), pinned and forced onto its software path; decode is the avkit-facing layer around it and the place where claims are measured. It is the only module in this organisation that produces pictures, and H.264 is its only codec.
data.limits#Limits: A stream is untrusted. Config.MaxFrameMBs (default 36864, a 4096x2304 picture) and MaxSampleBytes (default 64 MiB) are checked before anything sized by the stream is allocated. A bomb test asserts a refusal under a memory limit, and the avcC parser and both sample decoders are fuzzed with a committed corpus.
data.measured#How it was measured:
Every picture’s MD5 is compared with ffmpeg -f framemd5 -pix_fmt yuv420p, single thread.
ITU-T H.264.1 conformance suite (AVCv1): 81 streams tried, 73 give the same pictures as ffmpeg. 69 do with go.264 v1.12.0 as pinned; 4 more (MR2 to MR5_TANDBERG) only with the upstream fix oops1/go.264#2, which is not yet released. The other 8 are not claimed: 5 interlaced and 3 using FMO/ASO. 29 streams in the repository run in CI against ffmpeg’s MD5s. 5 real files (MP4 and Matroska, 720x300 to 1920x1080, x264), 900 pictures each, recorded as hashes.
data.speed#Speed: Not yet measured against ffmpeg, so nothing is claimed about it. It is tracked in go-avkit/decode#2.
data.using-it#Using it: r, _ := container.NewReader(file) frames, err := decode.DecodeTrack(r, trackID, decode.Config{}) for _, f := range frames { // display order use(f.Y, f.Cb, f.Cr, f.YStride, f.CStride, f.Width, f.Height, f.PTS) } Input: an avcC record (decode.NewAVCC) or a TrackConfig (decode.NewTrack) with length-prefixed samples, fed with DecodeSample and ended with Flush; or a raw Annex B stream (decode.New, DecodeAnnexB). Output: frames in display order, with planes, strides, size, chroma format, bit depth and PTS.
data.what-it-decodes#What it decodes: Profile State Constrained Baseline; Baseline without FMO/ASO bit-exact Main, progressive (CAVLC, CABAC, B pictures, weighted prediction, multiple and long-term references, MMCO) bit-exact High, 4:2:0 8-bit, progressive bit-exact on the streams measured; no JVT FRExt stream measured yet Interlaced (PAFF, MBAFF), FMO/ASO, Extended refused with ErrUnsupported High 10, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, lossless refused with ErrUnsupported

This table is kept by hand, and it had fallen six modules behind — it listed avkit alone while the organisation held seven. To check it, ask the organisation which of its repositories are Go modules:
for r in $(gh repo list go-avkit --limit 60 --json name --jq '.[].name'); do gh api repos/go-avkit/$r/contents/go.mod --jq '.name' >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "$r" done | sort
